Import cohort data

Source: vignettes/a02_import.Rmd
a02_import.Rmd

Import the configured study

getDataForStudy() retrieves the cohort records, cleans their intervals and saves the input for trajectory generation. It needs the study environment returned by cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration() and updates that environment after a successful import. It returns NULL invisibly; keep the environment for the call to createTrajectories(). See configuration if you have not created one.

CDM data

For a study configured with useCDM = TRUE, pass the connected CDM reference:

getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)

With a non-NULL baseUrl, the package downloads the selected cohort definitions from the ATLAS WebAPI. CDMConnector generates those cohorts on the supplied database and retrieves their records. atlasTargetCohort and atlasStateCohorts identify these definitions. Patient records come from the connected CDM database.

The target definition is stored as JSON/0.json. State definitions use JSON/atlas_<id>.json. The package creates CohortsToCreate.csv to map files to generated cohorts. Clinical labels are kept separate from these filenames.

The database account must be able to create and drop tables in its write schema. Generated cohorts use a unique package-owned name and are removed after their records have been collected. Existing tables are preserved, and the database connection stays open.

For an authenticated WebAPI, pass the required HTTP headers in the import call:

getDataForStudy(
  cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv,
  webApiHeaders = c(Authorization = paste("Bearer", Sys.getenv("ATLAS_TOKEN")))
)

Headers are used only for the download and are excluded from saved settings. No browser login is started. Use the header names and authentication scheme required by your WebAPI, or use local cohort JSON.

Use local cohort JSON instead of ATLAS

Set baseUrl = NULL and supply filenames without .json. Paths are relative to the study’s JSON folder. For this example, place target.json, states/A.json and states/B.json under local-json/JSON after configuration. They must contain the cohort expressions used to generate the cohorts.

studyEnv <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "local-json",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  useCDM = TRUE,
  baseUrl = NULL,
  atlasTargetCohort = "target",
  atlasStateCohorts = c(A = "states/A", B = "states/B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  cycleLength = 7
)

# Place the JSON files in the study folder before this call.
getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)

The package still generates cohorts on the CDM. Only the source of their definitions has changed. Relative subfolders are supported. Do not use absolute paths or parent traversal in definitions intended for saved replay.

CDM imports work in a temporary JSON folder. Downloads and the new manifest are published only after a successful import. Failed downloads, queries and empty eligible cohorts leave the previous working definitions unchanged. Unrelated JSON files are not replaced.

Local data

Set useCDM = FALSE to import a data frame or CSV without a database. Use these four column names exactly:

Column Content
subject_id Patient identifier. Use character values for leading zeros or large IDs.
cohort_definition_id Character label. "0" identifies a target interval. Other values are state labels.
cohort_start_date Interval start, as an R Date in a data frame.
cohort_end_date Interval end, as an R Date in a data frame.

For CSV input, write dates as YYYY-MM-DD. Dates must be present, with the end on or after the start. Intervals include both endpoints. Patient IDs must be present and nonblank. Numeric whole-number and integer64 IDs are also accepted. Use character or integer64 before creating values at or above 2^53 to avoid rounding in R doubles.

The target label is the text "0", regardless of the clinical labels. This example includes a second patient with a target interval and no state records:

rawData <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("001", "001", "001", "002"),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "A", "B", "0"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-08", "2020-01-01"
  )),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-21", "2020-01-07", "2020-01-14", "2020-01-21"
  ))
)

studyEnv <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "local-data",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = rawData,
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  cycleLength = 7
)

getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv)

To configure a CSV source instead, omit trajectoryDataObject and supply pathToData = "path/to/input.csv". The package reads patient IDs and state labels as text, preserving leading zeros and the literal label "NA".

Replace the input for one import

An explicit local source takes precedence over the configured alternative:

# Use this CSV even if the configuration contains a data frame.
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv, pathToData = "path/to/new-input.csv")

# Use this data frame even if the configuration contains a CSV path.
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = studyEnv, trajectoryDataObject = newData)

Do not supply both non-NULL sources in one call. With neither supplied, the configured data frame is used when present, otherwise the configured CSV is used. Set trajectoryDataObject = NULL in an import call to use the configured CSV instead. These overrides apply to that import only. CDM imports ignore both local source arguments.

What cleaning does

Only patients with a target row are retained. With the default targetEpisodeHandling = "First", the first target interval by start date supplies the bounds. State records are removed or clipped to those bounds. outOfCohortAllowed = TRUE lets retained records extend the target end, without moving its start.

With targetEpisodeHandling = "All", identical target intervals are deduplicated and each distinct interval becomes an episode. Overlapping target intervals are rejected, including a shared endpoint because dates are inclusive. Adjacent intervals are valid. States are clipped to every intersecting episode; no rows are created for gaps between episodes. This mode requires outOfCohortAllowed = FALSE. Set the period choice during configuration or pass it to getDataForStudy() for a fresh study; reimport to change it.

Overlapping records for the same patient and state are combined. Every label in stateCohortMandatory must occur within each retained episode. Eligibility is checked separately for every episode in "All" mode. Episodes with no state records remain eligible when there are no mandatory requirements. Episode numbers are assigned chronologically within the patient before eligibility filtering, so retained episode IDs can have gaps.

When mergeStates = TRUE, overlaps between different states are then represented by their structured membership, as described in configuration.

If no eligible patients remain, import does not succeed. Previous cleaned files are kept, and trajectory generation is blocked until a later import succeeds. Changing mandatory-state requirements also requires another import.

Saved studies

Restore a version 6, 5 or 4 snapshot with runSavedStudy = TRUE, then import fresh data. See saved-study configuration for the Settings-only sharing workflow. A saved CDM study uses the definitions embedded in the RDS file, without an ATLAS connection or working JSON files:

getDataForStudy(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = savedStudy)

For a saved local-data study, configure useCDM = FALSE and supply a new local source. The same per-call source precedence applies. Saved runs restore their analysis settings, so do not pass replacement labels, mandatory states, transition rules, episode handling or merging options. Versions 4 and 5 restore targetEpisodeHandling = "First" and stopAfterAbsorbingEpisode = FALSE.

After import, continue to trajectory generation. The output article describes cleaned data, trajectories and the saved settings file.
